bull_case: Heavy reinvestment in R&D, aircraft/logistics and facilities opens Kidney, Gen 3 and international expansion while route density and product scale restore owner FCF/share growth.
bear_case: The company is evolving into a capital-intensive logistics operator; capex, working capital, SBC and R&D absorb cash faster than per-share economics improve.
thesis: TMDX has an unusually large reinvestment runway and strong historical incremental economics, but current per-share cash quality has weakened. TTM capex plus R&D exceeds TTM operating cash flow, showing aggressive internal absorption, while SBC-adjusted owner FCF/share has fallen from the unusually strong 2025 level. This is consistent with a growth investment phase, but the strategy requires evidence that the spending converts back into per-share FCF.

evidence.claim: Using reported periods, TTM OCF is about $145.9M, TTM capex $66.9M and TTM R&D $92.5M, implying capex+R&D absorption of roughly 109% of OCF.
FY2025 revenue grew to $605.5M from $441.5M in 2024 and $241.6M in 2023, while OCF improved to $192.8M in 2025.
H1 2026 R&D rose to $56.5M from $33.1M, primarily for next-generation OCS, Kidney and clinical programs, while H1 OCF fell to $41.8M.
TTM raw FCF is about $79.0M; after roughly $37.1M TTM SBC, a conservative owner-FCF proxy is about $42.0M or ~$1.03 per Q2 diluted share.

counterevidence: 2026 capex includes growth real estate and strategic infrastructure rather than only maintenance spending.
Working-capital growth consumed $36.8M of H1 2026 operating cash flow and may partially reverse.
Product gross margins remain high and service gross margin improved, supporting future operating leverage.
Historical revenue and OCF expansion suggest prior R&D/NOP investment created substantial value.
unknowns: Normalized owner FCF after Somerville and fleet buildout.
Long-run aircraft replacement and maintenance capital.
falsifiers: If owner FCF/share does not recover despite revenue growth, incremental ROIC should be cut below cost-of-capital quality.
If Kidney/Gen3 convert R&D into high-margin revenue and working capital normalizes, FCF/share quality should be raised.
If capex+R&D remains above OCF for years without margin improvement, the reinvestment thesis fails.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: 2026 cash returns have weakened, but multi-year revenue/OCF growth and identified growth investments do not establish a structural collapse in incremental returns.
SBC is recurring and convertibles can dilute shares; current dilution is manageable but long-duration per-share impact remains unresolved.

subscores.rationale: 2023-2025 revenue and OCF scaled rapidly on prior investment, but 2026 margin/cash conversion pressure prevents an elite score.
TTM capex+R&D exceeds 100% of OCF and multiple internal growth avenues exist; prior returns support the high-absorption rubric condition.
Conservative SBC-adjusted owner FCF/share has fallen materially versus the strong 2025 level, so current per-share cash quality is weak despite plausible normalization.

uncertainties.rationale: Current investment has not yet matured into observable returns.
The runway is large, but some spending is infrastructure rather than directly scalable R&D.
Working-capital timing and growth capex make current owner-FCF normalization highly uncertain.
